Solved. Shah-Urschel, 'Entry growth in Gaussian elimination' (arXiv:2608.19189, Aug 2026), Thm 1.7: for every n a completely pivoted matrix has growth >= n^{(1/16-o(1))log_2 n}. That is superpolynomial, so g_n/n->inf and g_n>=n^{1+delta} both hold. It matches the BEU upper bound n^{0.2079 ln n} up to about 2x in the exponent; the authors say it settles the asymptotics.
